title: Run of the return-state simulation
statement: Let $M$ be a machine with $m$ work tapes, and embed those tape indices into $k$ work tapes. Start its $k$-tape simulation from the configuration obtained by placing its tapes at the embedded indices, supplying arbitrary contents and head positions on the other tapes, prefixing its output by a fixed word, and renaming each original state into a left-summand state. Suppose the initial configuration is not halted, every configuration reached by $M$ at a time $t<T$ is not halted, and the configuration at time $T$ is halted. Then, at every time $t<T$, the simulation agrees with the embedded configuration of $M$ with its state renamed into the left summand; at time $T$ it agrees in all configuration data except that its state is the distinguished right-summand state; and at all times $t<T$ its state is not that distinguished state.
hypotheses_covered: An embedding of the $m$ work-tape indices into the $k$ work-tape indices

The initial state of $c$ is not halted
Every run configuration at time $t<T$ is not halted
The run configuration at time $T$ is halted
